text:
alex: quick follow-up to the iterator/transport RFC — we need a concrete plan for SDK surfaces across Py/TS/Go before next sprint. main questions: do we deprecate sync iterators in Python, how do we expose resumable streaming (resume tokens vs pagination), and where do retries live (transport vs iterator layer)?
maria: short answer: prefer a single semantic model for users (a streaming/paginated view) and implement language-specific ergonomics. but details matter.
jonathan: +1. for Go and TS, sync vs async is less of a friction point. Python is the odd one because sync users expect blocking iterators. we could provide a thin sync wrapper around the async implementation and mark it as deprecated with a migration path.
tasha: prefer deprecation over removal. many infra customers still use sync loops. we should provide a compatibility shim for 6-12 months with telemetry to find adopters. :eyes:
cheng: transport-level retries should handle idempotent unary calls. for streaming (stream-of-tokens or stream-of-items) transport retries can't always restore semantics. propose: transport retries for connection-level transient errors, and operator-level checkpointing for resumable streams.
alex: agreed. sketch of API idea: single conceptual API: "stream_iter" that can be consumed as pages or as a continuous stream. examples: 1) async iterator -> emits tokens/messages 2) paginated API -> emits pages with resume_token. bind both to the same server-side resume token so switching is easy.
maria: sample pseudo-shape for Python:

```python
# async
async for event in client.responses.stream(request):
    handle(event)

# paginated
for page in client.responses.pages(request):
    for item in page.items:
        handle(item)
```

Keep `pages()` and `stream()` backed by same cursor.
jonathan: important: resume_token semantics must be idempotent and stable across model rollouts. server must guarantee token replays don't mutate state. implementation note: token encodes last-ok-offset + model-version-hash. if model changes, server returns `StaleResumeError` and client retries with conservative fallback.
tasha: +1. Also we need to define backpressure contract. if client stops consuming, server can pause and keep KV cache for X seconds. we should expose a `lease` TTL in resume token metadata.
cheng: on transports: gRPC streaming is our most efficient option for dedicated/private deployments. For hosted HTTP APIs (webapps) we need a robust HTTP/2 or SSE fallback. propose transport adapter interface:

```
interface Transport {
  requestUnary(req) -> Response
  startStream(req) -> StreamHandle
  onReconnect(h) -> void
}
```

Language SDKs implement Transport via gRPC, fetch+EventSource, or websocket. keep adapters small.
alex: retries: policy defaults: unary calls -> retry with idempotency header and exponential backoff. streaming start -> retry connect with jitter until TTL. in middle-of-stream errors -> if we have resume_token, resume from token and reconcile duplicates client-side. avoid re-delivery by providing sequence numbers on items.
maria: client-side dedupe pattern is necessary. provide optional helper `Deduper` that uses sequence numbers to drop duplicates. show in README.
jonathan: for Python sync wrapper, implement using `anyio`/`trio` or `asyncio.run`? prefer `anyio` to support both, but adds dependency. alternative: implement sync wrapper using background event loop thread with queue bridging — simpler and dependencyless.
tasha: background-thread bridging seems pragmatic. mark sync wrapper as deprecated and clearly document edge cases (blocking behavior, shutdown ordering).
cheng: telemetry: emit metrics when a resume happens, when resume tokens are stale, and when dedupe drops items. this will help tune TTL.
alex: plan for next steps:
1) write RFC follow-up that defines resume_token shape, idempotency guarantees, dedupe helpers, and transport adapter interface. 2) implement transport adapter in go/ts/py repo roots. 3) add sync shim in Python with deprecation header + telemetry. 4) add migration docs and code samples.

devx-bot: deployment note: integration tests for stream resume landed on staging. CI job `stream-resume-e2e` flaked twice in last 24h.
maria: thanks. I'll draft the follow-up RFC by EOD with those concrete API sketches and a migration timeline. tagging @jonathan @tasha for review.
jonathan: will review, focus on error semantics and sequence numbering details.
tasha: will write the deprecation copy and migration guide skeleton.
cheng: I'll prototype transport adapter and deduper helper. expect PR early next week.
alex: perfect. let's keep the follow-up RFC narrow: resume token shape, transport adapter, retries, sync shim policy, telemetry. goal: ship prototypes in 2 sprints. :rocket:
